messages.subject: custom strip function
parts:
Hi!

Is it possible to supply a custom strip function? I'd like print the strip label directly into some corner of the main plot. This violates some plotting rules, but gives me extra space in the plot. My first thought was to suppress the strips at all and work with geom_text instead. The problem here is that I have to supply the coordinates in native coordinates of my underlying data - but I would like to give a command like "write the text at the bottom right of the panel". There are grid functions doing this, but is this logic possible with ggplot2?

Maybe annotate does the job, but I could not find any documentation about it.

Thanks a lot.

Sebastian

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: custom strip function
parts:
Hi,

It would be nice to be able to re-define panel.background with a
function that is aware of which panel is being drawn (e.g. we could
paint the background with a different colour for each facet, or in
your case add a custom grob at a corner, ...). It's quite easy with
lattice, but I don't see how one would do that with ggplot2.

You could consider creating a geom that works in normalised parent
coordinates as opposed to native,

GeomTest <- proto(Geom, {

draw <- function(., data, scales, coordinates, ...) {
with(data,
gTree(children=gList(
rectGrob(x,y,default.units="npc",width=1.5*stringWidth(label),height=1.5*stringHeight(label),
gp=gpar(fill="grey90"), hjust=hjust,vjust=vjust),
textGrob(label, unit(x,"npc"), unit(y,"npc"),
default.units="npc", hjust=hjust,vjust=vjust))))

}

objname <- "test"

default_stat <- function(.) StatIdentity
required_aes <- c("x", "y", "label")
default_aes <- function(.) aes(hjust=0.5, vjust=0.5)
guide_geom <- function(x) "blank"


})

geom_test <- GeomTest$build_accessor()


p = qplot(x,y,data=data.frame(x=1:4,y=1:4,f=letters[1:2]), facets=~f)
+ theme_bw()

p + geom_test(aes(label=label), vjust=0, hjust=1,
data.frame(x=rep(1,2), y=rep(0,2), f=factor(letters[1:2]),
label=LETTERS[1:2]))

HTH,

baptiste
